extracted.intended_audience: newsroom journalists, editors and staff at Reuters / Thomson Reuters (and other news professionals seeking editorial standards)
extracted.subtask_description: Foundational editorial principles and actionable newsroom standards for producing and evaluating wire-service journalism emphasizing integrity, independence, accuracy, speed and global relevance. Derived from the Reuters Trust Principles and accompanying implications, style rules, and newsworthiness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity, independence and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrity, independence and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational Trust Principle (created 1941 to preserve Reuters' independence; codified in Reuters charter and Thomson Reuters founding documents). Applies at all times to editorial judgment and output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply unbiased and reliable news services
rubrics_metrics.description: Thomson Reuters shall supply unbiased and reliable news services to newspapers, news agencies, broadcasters, and other media subscribers, and to businesses, governments, institutions, individuals and others with whom Thomson Reuters has or may have contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates that services provided to a wide range of clients be both unbiased and reliable; emphasizes obligation to external subscribers and contractual partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand, develop and adapt services
rubrics_metrics.description: No effort shall be spared to expand, develop and adapt the news and other services and products of Thomson Reuters in order to maintain its leading position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and product teams should continually innovate and adapt to maintain leadership while adhering to the principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent control by any one interest, group or faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Thomson Reuters shall not pass into the hands of any one interest, group or faction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational ownership and governance must protect editorial independence; guards against capture by a single owner or faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management responsibility for maintaining principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Management shall act at all times with proper regard to the maintenance of these principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership and management have explicit duty to uphold and enforce the Trust Principles in decisions affecting editorial direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy is sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Implications for Newsworthiness' — accuracy is treated as a supreme obligation, prioritized even over being first to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and freedom from bias required in every story
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance and freedom from bias required in every story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every story must strive for balance and be free from bias; this is an operational expectation derived from the Trust Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images and stories must reflect reality (no manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and stories must reflect reality (no manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits manipulated images or fabricated details; visual and textual content must accurately represent events and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require openness and clear correction practices when mistakes occur; transparency is an explicit implication of the Trust Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldwide reach prioritized — global beats and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Worldwide reach prioritized — global beats and significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness emphasizes global relevance and coverage of international beats, reflecting Reuters' wire-service remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single owner can dictate editorial direction (implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: No single owner can dictate editorial direction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the Trust Principle prohibiting control by one interest; editorial decisions must remain independent of ownership pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, don't tell
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial style guidance: prioritize factual reporting and concrete evidence over opinionated narration or explicit editorializing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-source verification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require confirmation from multiple independent sources before publishing; part of derived editorial style standards to ensure reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-style speed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate with the speed expectations of a wire service while balancing accuracy; implies fast reporting workflows and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original reporting prioritized over commentary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial preference for original reporting and fact-gathering rather than opinion pieces or commentary when serving the core news mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution mandatory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reporting must attribute information to its sources; anonymity exceptions require justification and editorial oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid emotive language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain neutral, objective tone; refrain from using language that injects emotion or bias into reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance to global business / governments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness criterion: prioritize stories that matter to global business and government audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed — wire service tradition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion emphasizing rapid reporting consistent with wire-service heritage, balanced by accuracy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking news as core
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core editorial focus on covering breaking events promptly as a central part of the organization's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy over scoop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial priority to verify and be correct rather than to be first with an unverified or inaccurate story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from source pressure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must resist pressure from sources or subjects to alter reporting; independence is enforced by principles and attribution practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide audience relevance (not niche)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News selection favors stories with broad, international relevance over narrowly niche topics for the wire audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information published must be verifiable through evidence or reliable sourcing; underpins multi-source verification and attribution rules.
